reasoning: Both models agree the PKGBUILD and .SRCINFO are safe. The package downloads a prebuilt binary from the official GitHub releases with a pinned version (v0.81.5) and SHA-256 checksum, then installs it with a symlink. No malicious top-level code, no eval/curl|bash/obfuscation, no data exfiltration. This is a standard binary package pattern. The disagreement is solely due to a tool error (HTTP 400) in the qwen3-235b report when auditing README.md, which deepseek-v4-flash correctly identified as safe documentation. Per the rules, tool errors carry no verdict signal and should not block a safe ruling when the actual packaging files are clean.
disagreement_analysis: The qwen3-235b report failed to audit README.md due to an API error (HTTP 400 BadRequestError), causing it to return 'inconclusive'. The deepseek-v4-flash report successfully audited all three files and found them safe. The disagreement is not about security findings but about tool reliability.
coverage_issues: qwen3-235b: README.md audit failed with HTTP 400 error - partial tool failure
learnings: Tool errors (API failures, timeouts) on individual files should not force an 'inconclusive' verdict when the security-critical files (PKGBUILD, .install, patches) were successfully audited and found safe
README.md and other documentation-only files should be deprioritized in verdict determination - they cannot execute code during makepkg and should not block a safe ruling
The audit tool should distinguish between 'file audit failed due to tool error' and 'file audit found security concerns' when computing the final verdict
